chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hajjāl from some of our companions who said:

A man passed by Wadi Muhassir, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered him, after departing, to return and walk back. The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And he takes the pebbles for throwing at the Jamaraat from al-Muzdalifah or from the road; and if he takes them from his pack in Mina, it is valid.

key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: Al-Muzdalifah, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the night after Mina
key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: Throwing of the pebbles at the Jamaraat pillars
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Wadi Muhassir, a valley near Mecca associated with a specific ritual return during Hajj
key_terms.يَسْعَى: To walk back/return (performing the ritual of Sa'i)

ai.seo_question: Where can a pilgrim obtain the pebbles for throwing at the Jamaraat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural details of the Hajj rites, specifically addressing the timing of Sa'i in relation to the departure from Muzdalifah and the validity of using pebbles collected from various locations, including the pilgrim's pack. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility (*rukhsah*) within ritual obligations, ensuring that the physical act of stoning the Jamarat is not hindered by strict geographical constraints regarding the source of the stones.
